references.text: Jesus rebukes the disciples for being slow to believe what the prophets had said—the same unbelief described in verse 11. See [ref:Luk 24:25|Luke 24:25].
Even after the women's testimony was confirmed by some who went to the tomb, the disciples were still doubtful. See [ref:Luk 24:22-24|Luke 24:22-24].
Mark describes the same thing: when the disciples heard that Jesus was alive and had been seen by Mary Magdalene, they would not believe it. See [ref:Mark 16:11|Mark 16:11].
Even after two others had seen Jesus, the disciples did not believe them, and Jesus rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart. See [ref:Mark 16:13-14|Mark 16:13-14].

Thomas refused to believe the other disciples' testimony about the resurrection unless he himself could see and touch Jesus' wounds—a concrete example of the same unbelief with which the women's words were met. See [ref:Joh 20:25|John 20:25].

When the servant girl Rhoda said that Peter was standing outside the door, they did not believe her—they said she was out of her mind. The pattern repeats itself: women's testimony was dismissed as unbelievable. See [ref:Apg 12:14-15|Acts 12:14-15].

Sarah laughed within herself when she heard the promise that she would have a son—a reaction of unbelief toward a divine message, similar to the disciples' response. See [ref:1 Mos 18:12|Genesis 18:12].

Even when Jesus himself appeared to the disciples, they found it hard to believe out of sheer joy and wonder. Their unbelief persisted until Jesus gave them tangible proof. See [ref:Luk 24:36-41|Luke 24:36-41].
